label: weak, sparse: late original/delimiter steps in sequences starting with 0 (no clean rule)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.013% of steps) with weak, uniform magnitudes (median 0.118, max 0.21). It never fires at t<3. About 72% of its activation mass is in sequences whose first token is 0 (first_tok 0 has 21x lift; j and t are next at about 3x). Within those sequences it fires on original-phase steps t>=3 and on the <DEL> step, mostly when the input is j, h, s, k, r or <DEL>, and the prefix often contains 2 or e (top examples start 0 t e 2 2 ...). It rarely fires in the copy phase. The broad predicate (first token 0, t>=3, not copy phase) gets about 70% recall but under 1% precision: the overwhelming majority of matching steps stay inactive. Adding conditions on input token, prefix contents and orig(1)==t raises precision to at most about 40%, but recall falls to about 10%. I found no predicate that separates the active steps; the feature looks like a thresholded, weak conjunction of many prefix-token cues. Magnitude is highest (top quartile) on 0 t e ... sequences at the <DEL> step or the steps just before it.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=0 (+5.33), in_tok=j (+3.40), orig1=t (+3.22), phase=2 & out_tok=0 (+3.21), prev_tok=h (+2.87), orig0=t (+2.87). Lower it: correct=1 (-5.26), prev3_tok=- (-3.49), recall_idx=2 (-2.61), phase=2 (-2.42).
